html:
The Marra are an Aboriginal people of the Limmen Bight and the lower Roper River in south-east Arnhem Land, in Australia's Northern Territory. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country runs from the coast of the Gulf of Carpentaria inland along the rivers. They lived by fishing, hunting dugong, turtle and wallaby, and gathering yams and seeds, and shared ceremonies and marriages with their neighbours the Alawa, Ngandi, Nunggubuyu and Yanyuwa.

Settlers came late. The Overland Telegraph Line crossed the Roper in the 1870s, and cattle stations followed, with killings of Aboriginal people across the district. In 1908 a mission was founded on the Roper, now the town of Ngukurr, where Marra and other peoples settled. The Marra language has very few speakers left.
sum: The Marra are an Aboriginal people of the Limmen Bight and the lower Roper River in south-east Arnhem Land, in Australia's Northern Territory. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.
